documents.title: Guidelines for Using Artificial Intelligence Tools and Platforms in Connection with Academic Work
documents.summary: August 2026 Provost guidelines updating the 2023 guidance. They keep a university default that AI-generated content submitted for evaluation is cheating, allow AI for unsubmitted study work, and give instructors three model syllabus options.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines give a default ("may not submit content ... generated ... by GAI tools") but invite instructors to choose among three model options: General Permission, Selective Permission, General Prohibition. Because it offers tiers/templates and leaves the choice to instructors, it is coded delegates.

documents.title: Additional Guidance Regarding Generative AI in Connection with Academic Work (For Faculty)
documents.summary: August 2023 provost letter with tips for faculty: reinforcing integrity, allowing disclosure, using SafeAssign cautiously, and spotting chatbot traits. It sets no AI stance of its own.
documents.stance_why: The letter sets no rule on whether AI is allowed; it advises faculty ("if the instructor permits the use of GAI") and leaves the decision to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: Provost advises faculty to "Reinforce what plagiarism/cheating is" and why and their expectations; advice to explain expectations, closest to P09 (communicate expectations).
units.anchor: what plagiarism
units.frag_start: Reinforce
units.policy: Instructors reinforce what plagiarism and cheating are, why they are wrong, and their expectations for turning in original work.

units.why: Suggests a "declaration of honesty in your assignments", an integrity pledge; P29 (students own what they submit) fits better than P09 because it is a promise attached to submitted work.
units.anchor: Consider including a declaration of honesty in your assignments
units.frag_start: Consider including a declaration of honesty

units.why: "Allow students to disclose, if the instructor permits the use of GAI ... and explain how it was useful"; disclosure with submission, P24.
units.anchor: Allow students to disclose, if the instructor permits the use of GAI
units.frag_start: Allow students to disclose

units.why: "Require at all levels meticulous citing of peer-reviewed and published work" is about citing sources generally, not AI; P24 does not fit (not AI disclosure), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: meticulous
units.frag_start: Require at all levels meticulous
units.uncovered_note: Instructors require meticulous citation of peer-reviewed and published sources generally (not AI-specific disclosure).

units.why: Suggests draft submissions so staff "get to know students’ writing voice" and minimize unauthorized tool use; assessment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Consider allowing draft submissions prior to final submissions
units.frag_start: Consider allowing draft submissions

units.why: "Plagiarism detection tools are available and should be used if you suspect a breach"; SafeAssign use to identify misuse, P40.
units.anchor: should be used if you suspect a breach in academic integrity
units.frag_start: Plagiarism detection tools are available

units.why: "no tools that can reliably detect GAI-generated text and that false positives may put you in a very difficult position"; P39.
units.anchor: no tools
units.frag_start: Keep in mind that there are

units.why: "Be clear in your expectations and refer to learning objectives and grading rubrics" when assessing work; communicating expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Be clear in your expectations and refer to learning objectives and grading rubrics or criteria
units.frag_start: Be clear in your expectations

units.why: "When possible, ask students to present work they have done orally or in a public forum"; understanding check, P34.
units.anchor: ask students to present work they have done orally or in a public forum
units.frag_start: When possible, ask students to present

units.why: Describes chatbot traits (phrases not used in class) as cues to "better detect inappropriate use"; process evidence for identifying misuse, P40.
units.anchor: Look for phrases that were never used in the classroom
units.frag_start: Look for phrases that were never used

units.why: Advises encouraging "creative and critical writing prompts ... more analysis and synthesis rather than repeat facts" because chatbots cannot create new ideas; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Encourage creative and critical writing prompts in your assignments
units.frag_start: Encourage creative and critical writing prompts

units.why: Chatbots "can generate false citations"; "Spot-check cited materials to ensure that they exist"; spot-checks identify misuse, P40.
units.anchor: Spot-check cited materials to ensure that they exist.
units.frag_start: Look for originality in writing. Spot-check cited materials

units.why: "Chatbots do not produce error-free content. Seek out inconsistencies"; identifies misuse by inconsistency with course materials, P40.
units.anchor: Seek out inconsistencies and materials that do not adhere to course materials
units.frag_start: Seek out inconsistencies

units.why: "Require students to write within context using real or even fictitious scenarios" grounds work so AI is less useful; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Require students to write within context using real or even fictitious scenarios
units.frag_start: Require students to write within context

units.why: "there is no failsafe method to prevent plagiarism"; honest statement of limits tied to detection reliability, P39 as nearest.
units.anchor: there is no failsafe method to prevent plagiarism
units.frag_start: Remember, there is no failsafe method

units.why: "education about why integrity is important ... is key" and instructors’ human skills are the best defense; integrity education, not tooling. No type fits (P41, P57 not about this), so UNCOVERED.

units.frag_start: Your human skills as instructors continue to be
units.uncovered_note: Teaching why integrity matters, rather than detection, is the main defense against AI-enabled dishonesty.

units.why: Offers LAI Instructional Core staff assistance; faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: Assistance from the LAI Instructional Core professional staff is always available

notes: Course layer deferred; no school or computing policy found. The faculty letter (Aug 2023) predates and may be partly superseded by the Aug 2026 guidelines. Two UNCOVERED units (general citation of sources; integrity education as main defense). Model-language blocks are templates addressed to students, coded as policy of the template.
